title: Replacing a Pedestal Sink Pop-Up Assembly (This Old House)
summary: This Old House guides a practical replacement of a pedestal sink pop-up assembly. The video identifies the worn component as the entire pop-up unit housed in the pedestal, then walks through shutting off the water, disconnecting the hot and cold lines, and detaching the drain before removing the pedestal. It then covers disassembling the old pop-up to pass it through the sink, preparing and installing the new unit with plumber’s putty, threading and tightening the connections from beneath the sink, and finally aligning the popup rod with its linkage and restoring water to test the operation. The finish includes a note on how the new stopper reassembles to allow through-sink installation and a brief assessment of the result."

sections.title: Overview of the popup assembly and worn part
sections.description: Introduces the new popup assembly and explains the stopper’s up-down function; identifies the worn component as the entire unit inside the pedestal.

sections.title: Prepare to remove the sink: shut off water and disconnect supply
sections.description: Shuts off the water and demonstrates breaking the supply connections with a 5/8 inch open-end wrench while bracing the valve with pliers; aims to loosen the connection counterclockwise.

sections.title: Drain connection and pedestal removal
sections.description: Notes that the pedestal sits over a trap; locates the accessible nut behind the pedestal to loosen so the pedestal can be removed from the wall; mentions avoiding floor damage.

sections.title: Remove old pop-up and prep new unit
sections.description: Removes the old pop-up and introduces the new unit; explains that the stopper disassembles into two to pass up through the sink, and that the connection can be bottom- or top-fed.

sections.title: Disassemble and pass-through installation of the new unit
sections.description: Shows loosening the nut to separate the unit for passage through the sink, possibly using pliers, and discusses the old unit as removed for reference while preparing to install the new one; introduces the use of putty under the connection.

sections.title: Threading, tightening, and watertight seal
sections.description: Demonstates threading the new unit, catching the thread, and tightening the underside nut to create a watertight seal; emphasizes keeping the popup rod away from the wall to allow linkage connection.

sections.title: Final test and appearance
sections.description: Restores hot and cold water, tests the popup operation, and comments on the finish—praising the new assembly for its look and functionality.

featured_techniques.technique: Disassemble popup stopper to pass through sink (top/bottom options)
Shut off water and disconnect supply with 5/8 inch wrench while bracing the valve
Tighten underside nut to form watertight seal
Apply plumber’s putty under the connection
Align popup rod with linkage during tightening
